name: Whisky and cigar voice fad
summary: Smoking and drinking for a husky voice; the voice change is real in some smokers but is documented as disease.
lead: The whisky and cigar voice fad refers to the idea, discussed in some online circles, that smoking and drinking produces a deep, husky voice that is attractive. The sources reviewed contain no material on its history or on community discussions of it.

name: Deep voice masculinity meta
summary: The belief that a deeper voice signals dominance and masculinity; voice physiology is documented, the social claims were not examined here.
lead: The deep voice masculinity meta is the belief, found in looksmaxxing and related culture, that a lower voice pitch signals masculinity and dominance and so contributes to perceived attractiveness or status. The sources reviewed contain no community text or studies on these perceptions, so this article covers only the underlying voice facts.

name: Voice transformation software
summary: Software that shifts voice pitch or timbre, used for disguise, effects and content; no appearance-related evidence reviewed.
lead: Voice transformation software changes the pitch or timbre of a speaker's voice, in real time or in post-processing. Wikipedia describes voice changers as hardware or software that alters pitch or timbre or adds distortion, with software versions now very common and using many algorithms. The sources reviewed contain no community discussion of its use for appearance or content creation.

name: Podcast mic and EQ boost
summary: Close-miking and low-end EQ make a recording sound deeper; the speaker's actual voice is unchanged.
lead: A podcast microphone with an equalizer (EQ) boost is a recording setup in which a directional microphone is used close to the mouth and low frequencies are raised electronically, so that a recorded voice sounds deeper or fuller. It is discussed in voice-focused corners of appearance and self-improvement culture as a way to make a recorded voice sound more resonant.

name: Accent training
summary: Coaching to change or clarify an accent; linguists say it takes years, and its appearance value is unstudied.
lead: Accent training, also called accent reduction or modification, is structured study of a language's sounds, stress, rhythm and intonation so speakers can be understood more easily or sound closer to a target accent. Speech-language pathologists, acting coaches and linguists offer it, and speech-language pathologists do not regard accents as disorders.

name: Speech pacing apps
summary: Apps for practicing speaking speed; pace affects impressions, but the apps themselves are untested.
lead: Speech pacing apps are software tools that people use to practice the speed and pauses of their speaking. Pace is of interest in appearance and presence culture because listeners form impressions from it. Researchers distinguish speaking rate, which includes pauses, from articulation rate, which excludes them, and typical English speech runs at about four syllables per second, with a range of roughly 3.3 to 5.9 depending on context.

name: Public speaking course
summary: Structured speech training; linked to confidence, with little direct trial evidence on appearance-related outcomes.
lead: A public speaking course is structured training in delivering speeches to a live audience, offered by clubs, schools and commercial providers. It appears in self-improvement and presence-focused culture as a way to build confidence and delivery.

name: Ear training
summary: Music pitch-recognition practice; borrowed for voice pitch awareness with no appearance studies.
lead: Ear training is the practice of learning to recognize pitches, intervals, melodies, chords and rhythms by ear alone, a core part of formal music education. In looksmaxxing-adjacent voice discussions it is mentioned for pitch awareness, for example controlling vocal pitch.

name: Tongue stretching exercises
summary: Tongue stretches said to deepen the voice; the only trial is in stroke swallowing rehab, not voice.
lead: Tongue stretching exercises are exercises in which the tongue is extended or held in a stretched position, either by the person alone or with assistance. In looksmaxxing and voice-related discussion they are sometimes said to lower the voice, although that purpose is not what the exercises have been studied for.

name: Gym and loud lifting for voice
summary: Folk belief that grunting while lifting deepens the voice; nothing has tested it.
lead: "Gym and loud lifting for voice" refers to a folk belief that weight training, and in particular grunting or shouting while lifting, can deepen the voice. It circulates in voice-related corners of appearance culture, but no published study located for this article has tested it.

name: Antiperspirant
summary: Aluminium-salt sweat blockers, the everyday wetness and odor fix.
lead: An antiperspirant is a topical product that reduces sweating, most commonly using aluminium salts such as aluminium chlorohydrate. It differs from a deodorant, which targets odor rather than sweat output. In the United States antiperspirants are regulated as over-the-counter drugs, whereas deodorants are cosmetics; in the European Union antiperspirants are generally classed as cosmetics.

name: Deodorant
summary: Odor control, not sweat control; the basic scent-hygiene tool.
lead: A deodorant is a product applied to the skin, usually the underarms, to control body odor. It does not stop sweating, unlike an antiperspirant. Odor arises mainly when skin bacteria break down sweat, especially apocrine secretions that become active at puberty.
claims: Smell matters to how attractive you are perceived.
Skipping soap and deodorant gives an ideal natural scent after showering.
Rubbing lemon on the armpits improves scent.

name: Clinical strength antiperspirant
summary: Stronger-aluminium antiperspirants for heavy sweaters; a step before Rx.
lead: Clinical strength antiperspirants are over-the-counter antiperspirants sold with higher concentrations of aluminium salts than ordinary products, aimed at people with heavy sweating. Ordinary antiperspirants use aluminium salts to form temporary plugs in sweat ducts, and topical antiperspirants are listed as first-line treatment for hyperhidrosis in guidelines.

name: Aluminum chloride prescription (Drysol)
summary: Rx aluminium chloride for heavy sweating; first-line, mainly irritating.
lead: Drysol is a brand of prescription topical aluminium chloride solution used for hyperhidrosis, or excessive sweating. Aluminium chloride is a stronger version of the ingredient in regular antiperspirants, and guidelines list topical antiperspirants as first-line therapy.

name: Botox for underarm sweat
summary: Neurotoxin injections that switch off underarm sweat glands for months at a time, a clinician-delivered option with thin entry-specific research.
lead: Botulinum toxin injections for underarm sweat involve injecting a neurotoxin into the skin of the armpit to reduce excessive sweating (axillary hyperhidrosis). The toxin blocks the release of acetylcholine from nerve endings, which is the signal that tells sweat glands to produce sweat .

name: miraDry
summary: A microwave device that destroys underarm sweat glands in a clinic; studied in several trials, with rare but serious nerve-injury and infection case reports.
lead: miraDry is a non-invasive microwave device made by Miramar Labs that heats tissue in the armpit to destroy sweat glands. It has been cleared by the US FDA and Health Canada for axillary hyperhidrosis and is also used for underarm odor .

name: Axillary sweat gland suction
summary: Surgical removal of underarm sweat glands through small incisions, with only small registered trials behind it in our sources.
lead: Axillary sweat gland suction, also called suction-curettage or liposuction-type removal, is a minor surgical approach to underarm sweating in which sweat glands in the armpit are physically removed or disrupted through small incisions .

name: Glycopyrronium wipes (Qbrexza)
summary: Prescription anticholinergic wipes for underarm sweat, FDA-approved in 2018, with case reports of accidental pupil dilation in children.
lead: Glycopyrronium tosylate wipes, sold as Qbrexza, are single-use cloths containing a topical anticholinergic, applied to the underarms to reduce excessive sweating. The US FDA approved topical glycopyrronium for primary axillary hyperhidrosis in June 2018 .

name: Oxybutynin for sweating
summary: A bladder drug used off-label as a sweat blocker, with a placebo-controlled trial behind it and a full anticholinergic side-effect profile.
lead: Oxybutynin is an anticholinergic (antimuscarinic) medication approved in the US in 1975 for overactive bladder. It is also used off-label to reduce excessive sweating, increasingly since the 2010s .

name: Iontophoresis
summary: Low-current electrical treatment for sweaty palms and soles, in use since the 1950s, with a wider role in drug delivery and diagnostics.
lead: Iontophoresis is a method of delivering substances through the skin using a low-intensity electric current, with charged molecules moved across the skin by electrorepulsion and electro-osmosis . In grooming and dermatology it is mainly known as a treatment for excessive sweating of the palms and soles (palmar-plantar hyperhidrosis) .

name: Armpit shaving
summary: Shaving the pits to cut odor-holding hair; the one study found shaved and unshaved smelled the same.
lead: Armpit shaving is the removal of underarm hair at the skin surface with a razor. It is the most common form of hair removal in general, and its results last only hours to days. In looksmaxxing and grooming discussions it is proposed as a way to reduce body odor, on the reasoning that hair gives bacteria and sweat more surface to cling to.

name: Pit hair laser removal
summary: Laser to remove armpit hair for good; it cuts hair, but odor benefit is untested.
lead: Laser hair removal uses light absorbed by dark pigment to damage hair follicles. It has been FDA-approved in the US since 1997 and became widespread from the 1990s. Underarms are one area treated, and in looksmaxxing circles the procedure is discussed as a lasting way to reduce armpit odor by removing the hair.

name: Acid body wash (AHA/BHA) for pits
summary: AHA/BHA exfoliating wash on the pits to starve odor bacteria; plausible in theory, untested for odor.
lead: Acid body washes contain alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs) such as glycolic or lactic acid, or beta hydroxy acid (BHA, salicylic acid), which chemically exfoliate skin. In looksmaxxing discussions they are applied to the armpits on the theory that lowering skin pH and removing dead skin reduces odor-causing bacteria.

name: Benzoyl peroxide wash for body odor
summary: Acne antibacterial wash repurposed for pit odor; the mechanism is plausible but odor use is untested.
lead: Benzoyl peroxide is an oxidizer used mainly as an acne medication. It is sold over the counter and appears on the WHO list of essential medicines. In looksmaxxing and body-care discussions, benzoyl peroxide washes are applied to the armpits or body on the theory that they kill odor-producing bacteria.

name: Antibacterial soap (Hibiclens)
summary: Hospital chlorhexidine antiseptic wash used for pit odor; strong antibacterial, odor outcomes untested.
lead: Hibiclens is a brand of topical chlorhexidine skin cleanser, one of several chlorhexidine brands. Chlorhexidine is an antiseptic used to prepare skin before surgery, clean wounds and in surgical scrubs, and is sold over the counter in the US. In looksmaxxing and body-care discussions it is used as a body wash for underarm odor, on the idea that it reduces odor-causing skin bacteria.

name: Zinc-based deodorant (Zinc ricinoleate)
summary: Castor-oil zinc salt in deodorants that claims to adsorb odor; mechanism unclear, no trials.
lead: Zinc ricinoleate is the zinc salt of ricinoleic acid, a main fatty acid in castor oil. Many deodorants include it as an odor-adsorbing ingredient, meaning it is said to capture odor molecules rather than mask them or stop sweat. In looksmaxxing and grooming discussions it is mentioned as an alternative to aluminum antiperspirants.

name: Mandelic acid deodorant (Lume)
summary: An acid-based deodorant built on mandelic acid, made popular by Lume; plausible chemistry but no deodorant trials exist.
lead: Mandelic acid deodorant refers to underarm and body deodorants built around mandelic acid, an aromatic alpha hydroxy acid, rather than around aluminium salts or fragrance. The best-known example is Lume, a brand that markets a "whole body" deodorant and describes the acid-based formula as an odour-control product.
claims: An acid deodorant controls odour by acting on odour-causing bacteria

name: Lume whole body deodorant
summary: A viral acid-based deodorant sold for the whole body; popular, but untested in trials.
lead: Lume is a deodorant brand that markets a "whole body" deodorant, intended for use beyond the underarms, built on an acid-based formula using mandelic acid. The product became widely discussed on short-video platforms, and is the best-known example of a wider trend toward non-aluminium, acid-based deodorants.
claims: A deodorant can be used on the whole body, not just the underarms

name: Magnesium deodorant
summary: An aluminium-free deodorant using magnesium hydroxide; popular as a natural alternative, but no trials exist.
lead: Magnesium deodorant refers to aluminium-free deodorants that use a magnesium compound, most often magnesium hydroxide (the active in milk of magnesia), applied to the underarms to reduce odour. Wikipedia's deodorant article notes that milk of magnesia is sometimes used this way, and that some versions contain trace sodium hypochlorite, a bactericide.

name: Crystal deodorant (alum stone)
summary: A block of alum rubbed on skin as a natural deodorant; ancient use, but published evidence is limited to irritation case reports.
lead: Crystal deodorant, often sold as an alum stone or "rock crystal", is a block of potassium or ammonium alum, a hydrated double sulfate salt of aluminium, rubbed on damp skin to reduce underarm and foot odour. It is marketed as a natural, fragrance-free alternative to conventional deodorants.
